areas.name: Left console
areas.text: The panel to the pilot's left with the engine start switches, the fuel controls, the two radios and the oxygen controls.

panels.name: Engine start, fuel and systems switches (left console)
panels.text: The left console holds the switches that start the engine, shut off or move the fuel, steer the nose wheel brakes and trims, and run the aileron hydraulics.
panels.context: The manual says the engine can be started only from the front cockpit. The switches for the engine start are grouped on the left console of the front cockpit.

controls.name: Engine panel (STARTER, JPT LMTR, MASTER)
controls.text: This is the group of three controls that start the engine: the ENGINE MASTER switch, the JPT LMTR switch and the STARTER button. They are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual says the start is automatic: after the starter button is pressed, the starter turns the engine and the fuel and ignition follow by themselves.

controls.name: ENGINE MASTER switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The ignition, starting circuits and booster pump have no power.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The ignition, starting circuits and booster pump have power.

controls.text: This switch gives power to the ignition and starting circuits and turns on the booster pump that pushes fuel to the engine.
controls.context: The manual says the FUEL PRESS caution light goes out when the master switch is ON, because the booster pump then builds pressure.

controls.name: JPT LMTR switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The limiter is disconnected.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The limiter prevents the maximum jet pipe temperature from being exceeded.

controls.text: This switch turns on the jet pipe temperature limiter. The limiter keeps the exhaust from becoming too hot by cutting the fuel a little when the limit is reached.
controls.context: The manual says the limit is 756 degrees Celsius. With the switch OFF, the pilot must watch the temperature by hand. A guard protects the switch.

controls.name: ENGINE STARTER button
controls.text: Pressing this button starts the engine. The starter spins the engine up, then fuel and sparks follow by themselves.
controls.context: The manual says to press it for 2 seconds and release, then to move the throttle to IDLE when the engine reaches 10 percent speed. The engine normally lights within 4 to 12 seconds.

controls.name: FUEL SHUT OFF switch with guard

positions.name: OPEN
positions.text: Fuel flows to the engine (guard down).

positions.name: CLOSED
positions.text: The fuel valve is shut (guard and toggle up).

controls.text: This guarded switch closes or opens the valve between the fuel tank and the engine. Closed, no fuel reaches the engine. A guard protects it.
controls.context: The manual says it is used in emergencies and for maintenance. A closed valve makes the FUEL PRESS light come on.

controls.name: FUEL TRANSFER switch (PYL, TIP)

positions.name: PYL
positions.text: Fuel is moved from the underwing tanks.

positions.name: TIP
positions.text: Fuel is moved from the wing tip tanks.

controls.text: This switch chooses which external tanks move their fuel into the main fuselage tank: the underwing tanks (PYL) or the wing tip tanks (TIP).
controls.context: The manual says the underwing tanks should be used up first, then the tip tanks. The transfer uses air from the engine compressor to push the fuel.

controls.name: ANTI SKID switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The anti-skid system works.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The anti-skid system is off.

controls.text: This switch turns the anti-skid system on or off. The anti-skid works like ABS in a car and keeps the wheels from locking when braking.
controls.context: The manual says the anti-skid can be switched off only from the front cockpit. The game also has a switch in the rear cockpit.

controls.name: RUDDER TRIM switch

positions.name: LH
positions.text: Trim to the left, while held.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: No trim movement.

positions.name: RH
positions.text: Trim to the right, while held.

controls.text: Holding this switch to LH or RH moves the rudder trim tab to give a steady push to the left or right on the rudder. It springs back to the middle.
controls.context: Trim means a steady push, so the pilot does not need to hold the pedals. The manual says the switch in the rear cockpit overrides the one in the front.

controls.name: AIL SERVO switch with guard

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The aileron servo is connected.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The aileron servo is disconnected.

controls.text: This guarded switch connects or disconnects the hydraulic help for the ailerons. Without it the pilot flies the ailerons with muscle power alone.
controls.context: The manual says the AIL SERVO caution light shows when the hydraulic pressure for the ailerons is missing or the switch is OFF.

controls.name: Landing gear emergency handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle lowers the landing gear using the emergency hydraulic supply if the normal system fails.
controls.context: The manual says the emergency circuit is independent of the main circuit.

controls.name: Anti-G valve button
controls.text: The anti-G valve inflates the pilot's G suit during hard turns. This button on the valve tests it.
controls.context: The manual says the valve has a push-button test. The game has no click for it.

controls.name: ADF panel (early versions)
controls.text: A panel for the ADF radio compass, found in early aircraft versions only. The manual shows it in the picture of the side panels and does not describe it.
controls.context: The game does not offer a click for it.

controls.name: GROUND FIRE switch with guard
controls.text: The game names these controls 'Ground fire' and 'Ground fire guard'. The manual does not describe them.
controls.context: The guard protects the switch so it is not moved by accident.

panels.name: Oxygen controls
panels.text: These levers control the pilot's breathing oxygen: the supply, the mix with cabin air, and an emergency lever.
panels.context: The manual says the oxygen system is a low pressure system that supplies oxygen on demand, with a regulator in each cockpit.

controls.name: Oxygen power supply
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Oxygen Power Supply'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: The oxygen system itself is described in the manual as a system with two interconnected bottles and a demand regulator in each cockpit.

controls.name: Oxygen diluter lever (Normal / 100%)

positions.name: Normal
positions.text: Oxygen is mixed with cabin air.
The pilot breathes pure oxygen.

controls.text: This lever sets what the pilot breathes. NORMAL mixes oxygen with cabin air. 100% gives pure oxygen.
controls.context: The take-off checks in the manual say the diluter lever is set as required.

controls.name: Oxygen emergency lever
controls.text: The game names this lever 'Oxygen Emergency Lever'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: The ejection seat has its own emergency oxygen supply, described in the manual.

panels.name: SMOKE panel (MB-339A/PAN only)
panels.text: The smoke panel of the Frecce Tricolori version switches the smoke system on. With it the plane draws white and coloured smoke trails behind it.
panels.context: The manual says the smoke is made by two fuel and smoke tanks under the wings, and the push-buttons on the stick and the throttle start the smoke. The smoke panel is on the left console of the PAN version.

controls.name: SMOKE panel (PAN only, whole panel)
controls.text: This is the smoke control panel of the MB-339A/PAN. It has a MASTER switch and two enable switches, COLOR and WHITE.
controls.context: The manual says all weapon functions are off while the MASTER switch of the smoke panel is ON.

controls.name: Smoke MASTER switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The smoke system is off and the weapon system works.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The smoke system is on and the weapon system is off.

controls.text: This switch turns the smoke system on. With it ON the weapon system is off, and the smoke push-buttons on the stick and the throttle work for smoke.
controls.context: The manual says the switch allows the operation of the smoke system or of the weapon system.

controls.name: COLOR smoke enable switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Coloured smoke is not enabled.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Coloured smoke is enabled.

controls.text: This switch allows the coloured smoke. With it on, the push-button on the throttle starts and stops the coloured smoke.
controls.context: The manual says the left tank carries the fluid for coloured smoke. A green light near the gunsight shows when the colour smoke is on.

controls.name: WHITE smoke enable switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: White smoke is not enabled.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: White smoke is enabled.

controls.text: This switch allows the white smoke. With it on, the weapon release button on the stick starts and stops the white smoke.
controls.context: The manual says the right tank carries the fluid for white smoke. A green light near the gunsight shows when the white smoke is on.

panels.name: Radios on the left console (UHF COMM1 and V/UHF COMM2)
panels.text: The left console holds the control boxes of the two radios. COMM1 is the UHF radio and COMM2 is the V/UHF radio. Both are used for talking to other aircraft and the tower.
panels.context: The game's labels on these boxes are short, for example 'Frequency' or 'Mode', and do not say which of the two radios a knob belongs to. The manual describes each radio on its own. A radio shows its frequency on the instrument panel repeater.

controls.name: UHF (COMM1) control panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the control box of the UHF radio COMM1. The manual calls the radio AN/ARC-150. It covers 225.0 to 399.975 MHz and has 20 stored channels.
controls.context: The same left console also holds the V/UHF COMM2 box. Control of each radio is handed over with the CONTROL SHIFT buttons.

controls.name: V/UHF (COMM2) control panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the control box of the V/UHF radio COMM2. The manual calls the radio SRT-651/N. It covers VHF and UHF frequencies and has 99 stored channels.
controls.context: The same left console also holds the UHF COMM1 box.

controls.name: Function dials (one for each radio)
controls.text: These two dials switch a radio off and choose how it works. On the UHF box, MAIN uses the main receiver and BOTH adds the receiver for the emergency channel 243 MHz. On the V/UHF box, T/R lets the main receiver work, T/R+G adds the guard receiver, and TEST runs a self-test.
controls.context: The game names both 'Function'. The manual says the ADF and DF positions do not work.

controls.name: Mode dials (one for each radio)
controls.text: These two dials choose how a radio is tuned: by hand with the frequency knobs (MAN), by a stored channel (PRE) or to the emergency frequency (GD for guard).
controls.context: The V/UHF box also has a 243 position that tunes 243.000 MHz and an LD position that stores a frequency in the chosen channel.

controls.name: Frequency selector knobs (five on each radio)
controls.text: These knobs set the radio frequency digit by digit. Each radio has five of them, from the hundreds of MHz to steps of 25 kHz.
controls.context: The frequency is the 'station number' of the radio. Both people must tune the same number to hear each other.

controls.name: Channel selector knobs
controls.text: These knobs choose a stored channel, like the station buttons of a car radio. The UHF box has one knob, labelled CHAN, for 20 channels. The V/UHF box has two knobs for 99 channels.
controls.context: The chosen number shows on the channel indicator.

controls.name: MEM button
controls.text: Pressing this button stores the frequency that is set on the knobs into the chosen channel.
controls.context: The manual describes the memory button on the UHF box.

controls.name: TONE button
controls.text: Pressing this button stops reception and sends a steady test tone on the chosen frequency.
controls.context: The manual says the tone is a continuous modulated signal.

controls.name: Squelch switches (one for each radio)
controls.text: Squelch cuts the hiss of a radio when nobody talks. These switches turn the cut-off on (SQL or SQ. ON) or off.
controls.context: On the V/UHF box the same switch also has a TONE position that sends a test tone.

controls.name: UHF modulation switch (FM or AM)

positions.name: FM
positions.text: On UHF frequencies the radio works in FM.

positions.name: AM
positions.text: On UHF frequencies the radio works in AM.

controls.text: This switch of the V/UHF radio chooses how a UHF signal is carried, FM or AM. It matters only on UHF frequencies.
controls.context: The pilot sets it to the type the other station uses.

controls.name: TOD selector (inoperative)
controls.text: This selector of the V/UHF radio is marked inoperative, which means it does nothing in the game.
controls.context: The manual lists a TOD selector among the V/UHF controls and says it is inoperative.

controls.name: BRT knob (V/UHF radio)
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the displays and the FAIL light of the V/UHF radio brighter or dimmer.
controls.context: The manual says it also adjusts the radio frequency repeater.

panels.name: Circuit breaker box No. 1 (left console)
panels.text: These circuit breakers are small push-in safety switches. Each one protects one electrical circuit and pops out when too much current flows.
panels.context: The manual describes circuit breaker boxes No. 1, 2, 4 and 5 for the crew, with the armament breakers partly in a box in the fuselage.

controls.text: This is the whole circuit breaker box No. 1. It holds a row of small push-in safety switches, one for each electrical circuit.
controls.context: Box No. 1 is one of the breaker boxes the manual names. The manual says boxes 1 and 2 are in the front cockpit, box 4 is reachable in flight only when the rear cockpit is occupied, and most armament breakers sit in a fuselage box that the pilot cannot reach.

areas.name: Right console
areas.text: The panel to the pilot's right with the audio panel, the navigation radios, the IFF box, the air conditioning and the lights.

panels.name: Audio and interphone panel (ICS)
panels.text: This panel is the volume and radio mixer for the pilot's headset. It switches on the radios the pilot wants to hear and sets how loud each one is. It also controls the intercom between the two crew members.
panels.context: The manual calls it the ICS-200 audio and interphone system. It has a panel on each right console, a push-to-talk switch on the throttle grip and a transmit button on the stick grip.

controls.name: Audio (ICS) control panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole audio panel on the right console. Its volume knobs, selector switch and call button are explained below.
controls.context: The manual says the system is powered directly by the essential bus.

controls.name: Receive volume knobs (COM1, COM2, ADF, TACAN, VOR/LOC, MARKERS)
controls.text: Each of these six knobs switches one receiver into the headset and sets its volume. Pulling a knob out turns that receiver on, and turning it sets the volume.
controls.context: COM1 and COM2 are the two radios. ADF, TACAN, VOR/LOC and MARKERS are the navigation receivers. The pilot hears their identification tones.

controls.name: Interphone volume knob (INT)
controls.text: Pulling this knob out and turning it sets the volume of the interphone, the intercom between the two crew members. Pulling it out is the hot microphone mode: the crew talks without pressing a button. Pressing it in is the cold microphone mode.
controls.context: In the cold microphone mode the talk happens only while the CALL button is pressed.

controls.name: Master volume knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the volume of everything the pilot hears in the headset, except the landing gear warning tone.
controls.context: The manual says the knob adjusts only the received signals.

controls.name: CALL button
controls.text: Pressing this button calls the other crew member on the interphone.
controls.context: The manual says that pressing it also raises the volume of the interphone and lowers the other signals.

controls.name: COMM1/COMM2 TX selector (transmitter selector switch)

positions.name: COMM1
positions.text: Transmission goes through the UHF radio COMM1.

positions.name: Centre
positions.text: The transmitters are not working.

positions.name: COMM2
positions.text: Transmission goes through the V/UHF radio COMM2.

controls.text: This switch chooses which radio the push-to-talk buttons transmit on. Forward is COMM1, the middle is rest, and backward is COMM2.
controls.context: The manual says the push-to-talk switch on the throttle can also be pushed forward or backward to pick the radio.

panels.name: AHRS/GPS control and display unit (CDU)
panels.text: This keypad and small screen belong to the navigation system that knows where the plane is (AHRS/GPS). The pilot types in waypoints and chooses where to steer.
panels.context: The manual says the unit can hold a flight plan of up to 99 points. Its steering information shows on the RDU and the HSI. The key letters here are the labels printed in the cockpit.

controls.name: AHRS/GPS control and display unit (whole unit)
controls.text: This is the whole AHRS/GPS control unit with its four-line screen, softkeys and keypad. Its keys are explained below.
controls.context: The manual says the unit displays up to 72 characters on four lines of 18. The data card slot is not reproduced in the simulation.

controls.name: AHRS/GPS system switch (IN GPS)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The AHRS/GPS system is enabled.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The AHRS/GPS system is disabled.

controls.text: This switch turns the AHRS/GPS navigation system on or off.
controls.context: The manual calls it the IN GPS switch.

controls.name: Softkeys (Row 1 to Row 4)
controls.text: These four keys sit beside the screen. Each one selects the line of text next to it, if that line starts with a '>' sign.
controls.context: The manual calls them softkeys. Which line each key picks changes with the menu on the screen.

controls.name: Number keys 0 to 9
controls.text: These ten keys type numbers, for example the latitude and longitude of a point.
controls.context: The numbers appear on the screen where the cursor stands.

controls.name: ENT key
controls.text: Pressing this key confirms a choice or accepts the numbers that were typed.
controls.context: The manual calls it the ENT key.

controls.name: CLR key
controls.text: Pressing this key deletes the last number typed. Pressed again it deletes more, and a third time it clears the whole line. On the first page of a menu it opens the DATA 1 menu.
controls.context: The manual says that before typing a latitude or longitude, it also switches between N and S or E and W.

controls.name: - / + selector
controls.text: This selector scrolls through the lists and menus with several pages, one line at a time. With the BRT key it also changes the brightness of the screen.
controls.context: The manual calls it the minus-plus selector.

controls.name: BRT key
controls.text: Pressing this key lets the minus-plus selector change the brightness of the display.
controls.context: The manual says the BRT key and the selector together adjust the display brightness.

controls.name: SET key
controls.text: Pressing this key moves the cursor on the lines of the screen.
controls.context: The manual describes the SET key as the one that moves the cursor.

controls.name: FLT PLN key
controls.text: Pressing this key opens the menu for the flight plan, where the pilot can use the flight plan or change the point to steer to.
controls.context: A flight plan is the list of points the plane is to fly to, in order.

controls.name: STEER key
controls.text: Pressing this key opens the menu for choosing the steerpoint by hand, the point the plane should steer to.
controls.context: The manual says the points can be waypoints, beacons, airports and intercept points. Pressing STEER shows the closest ones first.

controls.name: MODE key
controls.text: Pressing this key opens the menu for choosing the operating mode of the navigation system.
controls.context: The manual lists it with the other menu keys: FIX, MARK, MODE, STEER, FLT PLN and SET.

controls.name: MARK key
controls.text: Pressing this key stores the present position as a mark point. The manual says up to 10 mark points can be stored.
controls.context: A mark point is a position the pilot wants to remember, for example a target seen in passing.

controls.name: FIX key
controls.text: Pressing this key would correct the position of the navigation system. The manual says this function is not reproduced in the simulation.
controls.context: The manual says position updating by fix is possible only in the dead reckoning mode.

panels.name: TACAN, VOR/ILS and navigation radio controls
panels.text: These control boxes on the right console tune the navigation radios: TACAN gives direction and distance to a station, and VOR/ILS gives a direction to a beacon or a landing line to a runway.
panels.context: The signals show on the HSI, the ADI and the RDU. Each cockpit has its own boxes, and the CONTROL SHIFT buttons decide which cockpit has control.

controls.name: TACAN control panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the whole TACAN control box. TACAN gives the pilot the direction and the distance to a ground or ship station that has been tuned in.
controls.context: The manual calls the equipment AN/ARN-118(V). It offers 126 channels, each in an X and a Y version.

controls.name: TACAN channel selectors (tens and units)
controls.text: These two knobs set the TACAN channel number. The left one sets the tens, the right one the units.
controls.context: The channel is the 'number' of the station. The CHANNEL window shows it.

controls.name: TACAN X/Y selector
controls.text: Turning this knob shows X or Y in the channel window. Ground stations use either the X or the Y version of a channel.
controls.context: The pilot must pick the one the station uses.

controls.name: TACAN mode selector

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: TACAN is off.

positions.name: REC
positions.text: The set receives and shows the bearing to the station.

positions.name: T/R
positions.text: The set also measures the distance to the station.

positions.name: A/A REC
positions.text: Bearing to another aircraft.

positions.name: A/A T/R
positions.text: Bearing and distance to another aircraft.

controls.text: This selector switches TACAN off or chooses what it does: receive only, receive and measure the distance, or the same with another aircraft instead of a ground station.
controls.context: The T/R position gives distance and bearing. In the air-to-air modes the two aircraft must be on channels 63 apart.

controls.name: VOR/ILS control panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the whole VOR/ILS control box. It tunes the VOR beacons and the ILS runway beams, and receives the marker beacons.
controls.context: The manual says the equipment covers 108.00 to 117.95 MHz for VOR and localizer, and 329.15 to 335.00 MHz for the glide path.

controls.name: VOR/ILS PWR switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The receiver is off.

positions.name: PWR
positions.text: The receiver is on.

controls.text: This switch turns the VOR/ILS receiver on. With it on, the VOR or localizer and the marker beacon functions work.
controls.context: The manual says the switch positions are OFF and PWR.

controls.name: VOR/ILS frequency knobs (1 MHz and 50 kHz)
controls.text: These two knobs tune the VOR or ILS frequency. One sets the whole MHz (three digits), the other the steps of 50 kHz.
controls.context: A VOR is a ground radio beacon. The pilot reads the direction to it on the HSI.

controls.name: test button (first)
controls.text: The game names this button 'test'. The TACAN box and the VOR/ILS box each have a test button, and the game's label does not say which one this is. This is the first of the two (callout PNT_158 in the front cockpit).
controls.context: The manual says the TACAN test button runs a self-test of the TACAN set, and the VOR/ILS test button does the VOR and ILS self-test.

controls.name: test button (second)
controls.text: The game names this button 'test'. The TACAN box and the VOR/ILS box each have a test button, and the game's label does not say which one this is. This is the second of the two (callout PNT_166 in the front cockpit).
controls.context: The manual says the VOR/ILS test button does the VOR and ILS self-test, and the TACAN test button runs a self-test of the TACAN set.

panels.name: IFF control panel
panels.text: IFF is a radio box that answers 'who are you?' questions from radars with a code number. This panel switches it on, sets the codes and tests it.
panels.context: The manual says the transponder works on 1030 and 1090 MHz, and that in a seat ejection it switches to emergency by itself.

controls.name: IFF control panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the whole IFF control box. Its switches are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual names the equipment SIT-421 transponder.

controls.name: MASTER selector

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The box is off.

positions.name: STBY
positions.text: The box is ready, not answering yet.

positions.name: NORM
positions.text: The box works and answers questions.

positions.name: EMER
positions.text: The box sends an emergency reply to any question.

controls.text: This selector is the main switch of the IFF box. OFF switches it off, STBY readies it, NORM makes it work, and EMER makes it send the emergency reply.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot sets it to EMER before bailing out.

controls.name: ANT switch (TOP, DIV, BOT)

positions.name: TOP
positions.text: The top antenna is used.

positions.name: DIV
positions.text: The system picks the antenna by itself.

positions.name: BOT
positions.text: The bottom antenna is used.

controls.text: This switch chooses which antenna the IFF uses: the one on top, the one on the bottom, or both with automatic choice (DIV, for diversity).
controls.context: The antennas are on the nose and under the middle of the fuselage.

controls.name: Mode switches (MODE 1, MODE 2, MODE 3/A, MODE C)

positions.name: OUT
positions.text: The mode is off.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The box replies in this mode.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: Self-test of this mode (springs back).

controls.text: These four switches turn the IFF modes on or off, and test them. OUT is off, ON replies to questions in that mode, and TEST runs a self-test.
controls.context: The game names them Mode 1 control, Mode 2 control, Mode 3/A control and Mode 3/C control. The manual says mode C works only when mode 3/A is on.

controls.name: Mode 4 control and Mode 4 audio switches
controls.text: The game names these two switches 'Mode 4 control' and 'Mode 4 Audio'. The manual lists a mode 4 test switch and an audio-light switch and marks them inoperative.
controls.context: The manual says the mode 4 parts are inoperative in this installation.

controls.name: RAD switch (RAD TEST / OUT)
controls.text: This switch lets the IFF box answer special test questions from ground test equipment. OUT switches it off.
controls.context: The manual says the position needs a ground test set, and the test works only when the master selector is at NORM or EMER.

controls.name: IDENT-MIC switch

positions.name: OUT
positions.text: No special reply.

positions.name: IDENT
positions.text: A special reply is sent for about 20 seconds.

positions.name: MIC
positions.text: A special reply is sent for about 20 seconds each time the stick transmit button is pressed.

controls.text: This switch makes the IFF box send a special identification reply for about 20 seconds, so the radar operator can pick out this plane. In MIC the special reply is sent every time the radio button on the stick is pressed.
controls.context: OUT is the off position. IDENT springs back after it is used.

controls.name: CODE switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Code'. The manual lists a CODE switch and marks it inoperative.
controls.context: It belongs to the code controls of the IFF box.

controls.name: CODE switches 1 to 6
controls.text: These six switches set the code numbers that the IFF box sends back. The manual lists code selectors for the modes 1, 2 and 3/A and does not say which of the six switches is which.
controls.context: The manual says mode 1 codes have two digits and mode 2 and mode 3/A codes have four. For the mode 2 code the grid must be moved up.

controls.name: Press To Test lamps (3)
controls.text: The game names these three buttons 'Press To Test'. They test lamps of the IFF panel. The manual does not say which button tests which lamp.
controls.context: The manual lists the lamps TEST-GO, TEST/MON NO GO, REPLY (mode 4) and the ALT, KIT and ANT warning lamps.

controls.name: ELT switch (ON, ARM, TEST/RST)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The transmitter is on and sends the distress signal.

positions.name: ARM
positions.text: The transmitter is ready to start by itself after an impact.

positions.name: TEST/RST
positions.text: Self-test, or reset after an accidental start (springs back).

controls.text: This switch controls the emergency locator transmitter, a radio that sends a distress signal after a crash. In ARM it starts by itself after an impact. ON starts it by hand. TEST/RST tests it and also stops an accidental activation.
controls.context: The manual says the toggle must be pulled before it is moved between ARM and ON. The ELT sends on 121.5 and 243.0 MHz and, through satellites, on 406.025 MHz.

panels.name: Cabin air, anti-ice and exterior-lights controls
panels.text: These controls on the right console look after the air in the cockpit, the heating of the pitot tubes and engine intakes, and the lights.
panels.context: The manual says the cabin pressure and temperature system works by itself, and the pilot only sets the wanted temperature. The anti-ice heaters are switched on in icing conditions.

controls.name: CABIN TEMP selector
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the temperature of the cockpit air. It mixes hot air from the engine with cold air from the cooling unit.
controls.context: The manual says the knob is on the right console of the front cockpit.

controls.name: CABIN PRESS switch with guard
controls.text: This guarded switch controls the pressurization of the cockpit. The pilot uses it to let the cabin pressure out before opening the ram air scoop for fresh air at high altitude.
controls.context: The manual says the pressure system works by itself while the CABIN PRESS breaker is in and the RAM AIR SCOOP is closed.

controls.name: RAM AIR SCOOP handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle opens a scoop in the nose that lets fresh outside air into the cockpit, if the engine air becomes contaminated.
controls.context: The manual says that above 8000 feet the cabin pressure must be let out with the CABIN PRESS switch first.

controls.name: WINDSHIELD/RAIN RMVL switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The air flow over the windshield is off.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Hot air blows over the windshield.

controls.text: This switch blows hot air from the engine over the windshield to keep ice off it or to clear rain. OFF stops the air.
controls.context: The manual says it can also be used on the ground to improve the view in rain.

controls.name: Windshield demist switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Windshield Demist'. The manual does not describe it as a separate switch. It lists a demist circuit breaker.
controls.context: Misting means a thin layer of water on the glass that blocks the view.

controls.name: ANTI-ICE PITOT switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The pitot heater is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The pitot heater is off.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The heater is tested; ON shows on the indicator.

controls.text: This switch heats a pitot tube, a small tube on the nose that measures airspeed, so ice cannot block it. ON heats, OFF stops, TEST checks the heater.
controls.context: The manual says each cockpit has its own switch. The front switch also heats the angle-of-attack probe. The indicators show ON, OFF or stripes.

controls.name: ANTI-ICE ENGINE switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The air intake heating is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The air intake heating is off.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The system is tested; ON shows on the indicator.

controls.text: This switch turns on the heating of the engine air intakes, so ice cannot build up there. ON heats, OFF stops, TEST checks it on the ground.
controls.context: The manual says the test needs the engine to run above 65 percent with both generators working. On the ground the electrical heating does not work.

panels.name: Lights control panel (LIGHTS)
panels.text: This panel switches the lights: the instrument and panel lights in the cockpit, and the lights on the outside of the plane.
panels.context: The manual says the cockpit lights are controlled on each right console and the outside lights from the front cockpit. The front panel is the main one.

controls.name: Lights control panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole lights panel on the right console. Its knobs and switches are explained below.
controls.context: The manual lists the controls: LDG LT/TAXI LT, CONSOLE, FLOOD, BCN, NAV, INST, WARN, FORM LIGHTS and the red spot light.

controls.name: INST knob (instrument lights)
controls.text: Turning this knob turns on the lights inside the instruments and sets how bright they are.
controls.context: OFF switches the instrument lights off. The manual says the knob works together with the instrument panel lighting.

controls.name: CONSOLE knob (panel lights)
controls.text: Turning this knob turns on the lights of the control panels and sets their brightness.
controls.context: OFF switches the console lights off. The console lights are fed by the DC primary bus.

controls.name: FLOOD knob (cockpit flood lights)
controls.text: Turning this knob turns on the white flood lights that light up the cockpit and sets their brightness.
controls.context: The manual says the front cockpit has six flood lights and the rear cockpit has five, and they can be swivelled.

controls.name: FORM LIGHTS knob (formation lights)
controls.text: Turning this knob turns on the formation lights and sets their brightness. Formation lights are soft glowing strips that help pilots fly close together at night.
controls.context: The manual says there are six of them, on the nose, the tip tanks and the rear fuselage.

controls.name: WARN switch (BRT/DIM)

positions.name: BRT
positions.text: The warning lights are bright.

positions.name: DIM
positions.text: The warning lights are dimmed.

controls.text: This switch sets the brightness of the warning, caution and advisory lights, bright or dimmed.
controls.context: The pilot dims them for night flying.

controls.name: NAV STEADY/FLASH switch

positions.name: STEADY
positions.text: The navigation lights shine steadily.

positions.name: FLASH
positions.text: The tail and wing tip lights flash.

controls.text: This switch chooses whether the tail and wing tip navigation lights shine steadily or flash.
controls.context: Navigation lights are the red, green and white lights that show other pilots which way the plane is heading.

controls.name: NAV BRT/OFF/DIM switch

positions.name: BRT
positions.text: The navigation lights are on at full brightness.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The navigation lights are off.

positions.name: DIM
positions.text: The navigation lights are on but dimmed.

controls.text: This switch turns the navigation lights on at full brightness (BRT), off (OFF) or dimmed (DIM).
controls.context: The manual says the plane has five navigation lights: two wing tip lights, a tail light and two fuselage lights.

controls.name: BCN switch (anti-collision beacon)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The anti-collision light is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The anti-collision light is off.

controls.text: This switch turns on the flashing anti-collision light on the tail fin, so other aircraft can see the plane.
controls.context: The manual says to switch it off near other aircraft at night to avoid blinding them.

panels.name: Circuit breaker box No. 2 (right console)
panels.text: These circuit breakers are small push-in safety switches. Each one protects one electrical circuit and pops out when too much current flows.
panels.context: The manual describes circuit breaker boxes No. 1, 2, 4 and 5 for the crew, with the armament breakers partly in a box in the fuselage.

controls.text: This is the whole circuit breaker box No. 5. It holds a row of small push-in safety switches, one for each electrical circuit.
controls.context: Box No. 5 is one of the breaker boxes the manual names. The manual says boxes 1 and 2 are in the front cockpit, box 4 is reachable in flight only when the rear cockpit is occupied, and most armament breakers sit in a fuselage box that the pilot cannot reach.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: lateral panels and centre stand
areas.text: The rear copies of the landing gear lever, the brakes, the control shift buttons, the canopy and the ejection seat handles.

panels.name: Landing gear, brakes and lights (left lateral panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The panel at the lower left of the instrument panel holds the landing gear lever, the brake handle, the lights switch and a few indicators.
panels.context: The pilot uses it on every take-off and landing: gear up after take-off, gear down before landing. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Landing gear lever

positions.name: LG UP
positions.text: The wheels are raised.

positions.name: LG DOWN
positions.text: The wheels are lowered and locked.

controls.text: Moving this lever up raises the wheels into the plane, and moving it down lets them come down. Three lights show whether each leg is down and locked. A red light in the handle shows when the gear and the lever do not agree.
controls.context: The manual says the gear may stay down up to 175 knots. A lock stops the lever from going up while the plane's weight is on the wheels. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: DOWNLOCK OVERRIDE button
controls.text: Pressing this button frees the landing gear lever so that the wheels can be raised even on the ground.
controls.context: Normally a lock holds the lever in DOWN while the plane's weight is on the wheels. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: FUEL DUMP switch

positions.name: Closed
positions.text: The dump valve is closed.

positions.name: Activated
positions.text: The switch is turned a quarter turn clockwise; the dump valve is open and fuel is let out.

controls.text: Turning this switch a quarter turn opens the dump valve, and the fuel is let out of the tanks into the air. Turning it back closes the valve.
controls.context: The manual says fuel dumping can be controlled in each cockpit alone, and the valve must be shut before landing. It is used in emergencies, to make the plane lighter. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: Electrical supply and warning panel (right lateral panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The panel at the lower right holds the electrical switches, the generator load gauges, the warning lights test and the caution lights panel.
panels.context: The pilot switches it on first when climbing in. The plane has two batteries, two generators and two inverters (they make alternating current). This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: CONTROL SHIFT buttons (COMM1, COMM2, ADF, VOR-ILS, TACAN, NAV)
controls.text: These six push-buttons hand control of a radio over to this cockpit. A lit button shows that this cockpit controls that equipment. The other pilot must press his own button to take control back.
controls.context: Two pilots share one set of radios, so only one cockpit controls each at a time. The manual states that the control cannot be handed back by pressing the same button again. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: Canopy, ejection seat and cockpit equipment (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These are the parts for getting in and out and for the safety of the crew: the canopy handles, the ejection seat handle and its safety pins, the mirrors and the glove compartment.
panels.context: The manual says the canopy opens to the right. The seat is a Martin-Baker Mk IT-10F ejection seat that works from zero speed and zero height. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Canopy handle
controls.text: This handle on the left inside of the canopy works the eight latches that lock the canopy shut. Moving it locks or unlocks the canopy.
controls.context: A CANOPY warning light on the instrument panel shows when the canopy is not locked. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Canopy lock/unlock
controls.text: The game names this control 'Canopy lock/unlock'. The manual does not describe it separately from the canopy handle.
controls.context: The manual says the canopy may be closed or partially open and locked in an intermediate position during taxi. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Canopy severance handles with safety pins (fwd, aft)
controls.text: Pulling this handle sets off an explosive cord around the edge of the canopy glass and shatters it. A safety pin keeps the handle from being pulled by accident.
controls.context: The manual says this device can be used by the crew or by ground helpers to get out. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Seat firing handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle fires the ejection seat. The seat and pilot leave the plane. The parachute opens by itself.
controls.context: It is the last resort. The manual says to hold the stick with one hand while pulling the handle with the other. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Seat height switch
controls.text: This switch moves the seat up or down with an electric motor, to suit the pilot's height.
controls.context: The seat height is set before engine start. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Mirrors open/close
controls.text: Clicking this control opens or folds away one of the rear-view mirrors of the cockpit. They help the pilot see behind the plane.
controls.context: The manual says the cockpit has mirrors that meet an American military standard. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Glove compartment
controls.text: Clicking this control opens a storage compartment in the cockpit, where maps and papers can be kept.
controls.context: The manual says there are four compartments in the cockpit for maps and documents. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: left console
areas.text: The rear copies of the fuel, trim, radio and oxygen controls.

panels.name: Engine start, fuel and systems switches (left console) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The left console holds the switches that start the engine, shut off or move the fuel, steer the nose wheel brakes and trims, and run the aileron hydraulics.
panels.context: The manual says the engine can be started only from the front cockpit. The switches for the engine start are grouped on the left console of the front cockpit. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: FUEL SHUT OFF switch with guard

positions.name: OPEN
positions.text: Fuel flows to the engine (guard down).

positions.name: CLOSED
positions.text: The fuel valve is shut (guard and toggle up).

controls.text: This guarded switch closes or opens the valve between the fuel tank and the engine. Closed, no fuel reaches the engine. A guard protects it.
controls.context: The manual says it is used in emergencies and for maintenance. A closed valve makes the FUEL PRESS light come on. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: ANTI SKID switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The anti-skid system works.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The anti-skid system is off.

controls.text: This switch turns the anti-skid system on or off. The anti-skid works like ABS in a car and keeps the wheels from locking when braking.
controls.context: The manual says the anti-skid can be switched off only from the front cockpit. The game also has a switch in the rear cockpit. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: RUDDER TRIM switch

positions.name: LH
positions.text: Trim to the left, while held.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: No trim movement.

positions.name: RH
positions.text: Trim to the right, while held.

controls.text: Holding this switch to LH or RH moves the rudder trim tab to give a steady push to the left or right on the rudder. It springs back to the middle.
controls.context: Trim means a steady push, so the pilot does not need to hold the pedals. The manual says the switch in the rear cockpit overrides the one in the front. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: AIL SERVO switch with guard

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The aileron servo is connected.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The aileron servo is disconnected.

controls.text: This guarded switch connects or disconnects the hydraulic help for the ailerons. Without it the pilot flies the ailerons with muscle power alone.
controls.context: The manual says the AIL SERVO caution light shows when the hydraulic pressure for the ailerons is missing or the switch is OFF. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: Oxygen controls (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These levers control the pilot's breathing oxygen: the supply, the mix with cabin air, and an emergency lever.
panels.context: The manual says the oxygen system is a low pressure system that supplies oxygen on demand, with a regulator in each cockpit. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Oxygen power supply
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Oxygen Power Supply'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: The oxygen system itself is described in the manual as a system with two interconnected bottles and a demand regulator in each cockpit. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Oxygen diluter lever (Normal / 100%)

positions.name: Normal
positions.text: Oxygen is mixed with cabin air.
The pilot breathes pure oxygen.

controls.text: This lever sets what the pilot breathes. NORMAL mixes oxygen with cabin air. 100% gives pure oxygen.
controls.context: The take-off checks in the manual say the diluter lever is set as required. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Oxygen emergency lever
controls.text: The game names this lever 'Oxygen Emergency Lever'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: The ejection seat has its own emergency oxygen supply, described in the manual. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: Radios on the left console (UHF COMM1 and V/UHF COMM2) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The left console holds the control boxes of the two radios. COMM1 is the UHF radio and COMM2 is the V/UHF radio. Both are used for talking to other aircraft and the tower.
panels.context: The game's labels on these boxes are short, for example 'Frequency' or 'Mode', and do not say which of the two radios a knob belongs to. The manual describes each radio on its own. A radio shows its frequency on the instrument panel repeater. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Function dials (one for each radio)
controls.text: These two dials switch a radio off and choose how it works. On the UHF box, MAIN uses the main receiver and BOTH adds the receiver for the emergency channel 243 MHz. On the V/UHF box, T/R lets the main receiver work, T/R+G adds the guard receiver, and TEST runs a self-test.
controls.context: The game names both 'Function'. The manual says the ADF and DF positions do not work. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Mode dials (one for each radio)
controls.text: These two dials choose how a radio is tuned: by hand with the frequency knobs (MAN), by a stored channel (PRE) or to the emergency frequency (GD for guard).
controls.context: The V/UHF box also has a 243 position that tunes 243.000 MHz and an LD position that stores a frequency in the chosen channel. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Frequency selector knobs (five on each radio)
controls.text: These knobs set the radio frequency digit by digit. Each radio has five of them, from the hundreds of MHz to steps of 25 kHz.
controls.context: The frequency is the 'station number' of the radio. Both people must tune the same number to hear each other. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Channel selector knobs
controls.text: These knobs choose a stored channel, like the station buttons of a car radio. The UHF box has one knob, labelled CHAN, for 20 channels. The V/UHF box has two knobs for 99 channels.
controls.context: The chosen number shows on the channel indicator. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: MEM button
controls.text: Pressing this button stores the frequency that is set on the knobs into the chosen channel.
controls.context: The manual describes the memory button on the UHF box. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: TONE button
controls.text: Pressing this button stops reception and sends a steady test tone on the chosen frequency.
controls.context: The manual says the tone is a continuous modulated signal. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Squelch switches (one for each radio)
controls.text: Squelch cuts the hiss of a radio when nobody talks. These switches turn the cut-off on (SQL or SQ. ON) or off.
controls.context: On the V/UHF box the same switch also has a TONE position that sends a test tone. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: UHF modulation switch (FM or AM)

positions.name: FM
positions.text: On UHF frequencies the radio works in FM.

positions.name: AM
positions.text: On UHF frequencies the radio works in AM.

controls.text: This switch of the V/UHF radio chooses how a UHF signal is carried, FM or AM. It matters only on UHF frequencies.
controls.context: The pilot sets it to the type the other station uses. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: TOD selector (inoperative)
controls.text: This selector of the V/UHF radio is marked inoperative, which means it does nothing in the game.
controls.context: The manual lists a TOD selector among the V/UHF controls and says it is inoperative. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: BRT knob (V/UHF radio)
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the displays and the FAIL light of the V/UHF radio brighter or dimmer.
controls.context: The manual says it also adjusts the radio frequency repeater. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: right console
areas.text: The rear copies of the audio panel, the navigation radios, the air conditioning and the lights.

panels.name: Audio and interphone panel (ICS) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel is the volume and radio mixer for the pilot's headset. It switches on the radios the pilot wants to hear and sets how loud each one is. It also controls the intercom between the two crew members.
panels.context: The manual calls it the ICS-200 audio and interphone system. It has a panel on each right console, a push-to-talk switch on the throttle grip and a transmit button on the stick grip. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Receive volume knobs (COM1, COM2, ADF, TACAN, VOR/LOC, MARKERS)
controls.text: Each of these six knobs switches one receiver into the headset and sets its volume. Pulling a knob out turns that receiver on, and turning it sets the volume.
controls.context: COM1 and COM2 are the two radios. ADF, TACAN, VOR/LOC and MARKERS are the navigation receivers. The pilot hears their identification tones. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Interphone volume knob (INT)
controls.text: Pulling this knob out and turning it sets the volume of the interphone, the intercom between the two crew members. Pulling it out is the hot microphone mode: the crew talks without pressing a button. Pressing it in is the cold microphone mode.
controls.context: In the cold microphone mode the talk happens only while the CALL button is pressed. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Master volume knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the volume of everything the pilot hears in the headset, except the landing gear warning tone.
controls.context: The manual says the knob adjusts only the received signals. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: CALL button
controls.text: Pressing this button calls the other crew member on the interphone.
controls.context: The manual says that pressing it also raises the volume of the interphone and lowers the other signals. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: COMM1/COMM2 TX selector (transmitter selector switch)

positions.name: COMM1
positions.text: Transmission goes through the UHF radio COMM1.

positions.name: Centre
positions.text: The transmitters are not working.

positions.name: COMM2
positions.text: Transmission goes through the V/UHF radio COMM2.

controls.text: This switch chooses which radio the push-to-talk buttons transmit on. Forward is COMM1, the middle is rest, and backward is COMM2.
controls.context: The manual says the push-to-talk switch on the throttle can also be pushed forward or backward to pick the radio. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: AHRS/GPS control and display unit (CDU) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This keypad and small screen belong to the navigation system that knows where the plane is (AHRS/GPS). The pilot types in waypoints and chooses where to steer.
panels.context: The manual says the unit can hold a flight plan of up to 99 points. Its steering information shows on the RDU and the HSI. The key letters here are the labels printed in the cockpit. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Softkeys (Row 1 to Row 4)
controls.text: These four keys sit beside the screen. Each one selects the line of text next to it, if that line starts with a '>' sign.
controls.context: The manual calls them softkeys. Which line each key picks changes with the menu on the screen. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Number keys 0 to 9
controls.text: These ten keys type numbers, for example the latitude and longitude of a point.
controls.context: The numbers appear on the screen where the cursor stands. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: ENT key
controls.text: Pressing this key confirms a choice or accepts the numbers that were typed.
controls.context: The manual calls it the ENT key. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: CLR key
controls.text: Pressing this key deletes the last number typed. Pressed again it deletes more, and a third time it clears the whole line. On the first page of a menu it opens the DATA 1 menu.
controls.context: The manual says that before typing a latitude or longitude, it also switches between N and S or E and W. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: - / + selector
controls.text: This selector scrolls through the lists and menus with several pages, one line at a time. With the BRT key it also changes the brightness of the screen.
controls.context: The manual calls it the minus-plus selector. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: BRT key
controls.text: Pressing this key lets the minus-plus selector change the brightness of the display.
controls.context: The manual says the BRT key and the selector together adjust the display brightness. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: SET key
controls.text: Pressing this key moves the cursor on the lines of the screen.
controls.context: The manual describes the SET key as the one that moves the cursor. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: FLT PLN key
controls.text: Pressing this key opens the menu for the flight plan, where the pilot can use the flight plan or change the point to steer to.
controls.context: A flight plan is the list of points the plane is to fly to, in order. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: STEER key
controls.text: Pressing this key opens the menu for choosing the steerpoint by hand, the point the plane should steer to.
controls.context: The manual says the points can be waypoints, beacons, airports and intercept points. Pressing STEER shows the closest ones first. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: MODE key
controls.text: Pressing this key opens the menu for choosing the operating mode of the navigation system.
controls.context: The manual lists it with the other menu keys: FIX, MARK, MODE, STEER, FLT PLN and SET. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: MARK key
controls.text: Pressing this key stores the present position as a mark point. The manual says up to 10 mark points can be stored.
controls.context: A mark point is a position the pilot wants to remember, for example a target seen in passing. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: FIX key
controls.text: Pressing this key would correct the position of the navigation system. The manual says this function is not reproduced in the simulation.
controls.context: The manual says position updating by fix is possible only in the dead reckoning mode. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: TACAN, VOR/ILS and navigation radio controls (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These control boxes on the right console tune the navigation radios: TACAN gives direction and distance to a station, and VOR/ILS gives a direction to a beacon or a landing line to a runway.
panels.context: The signals show on the HSI, the ADI and the RDU. Each cockpit has its own boxes, and the CONTROL SHIFT buttons decide which cockpit has control. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: TACAN channel selectors (tens and units)
controls.text: These two knobs set the TACAN channel number. The left one sets the tens, the right one the units.
controls.context: The channel is the 'number' of the station. The CHANNEL window shows it. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: TACAN X/Y selector
controls.text: Turning this knob shows X or Y in the channel window. Ground stations use either the X or the Y version of a channel.
controls.context: The pilot must pick the one the station uses. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: TACAN mode selector

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: TACAN is off.

positions.name: REC
positions.text: The set receives and shows the bearing to the station.

positions.name: T/R
positions.text: The set also measures the distance to the station.

positions.name: A/A REC
positions.text: Bearing to another aircraft.

positions.name: A/A T/R
positions.text: Bearing and distance to another aircraft.

controls.text: This selector switches TACAN off or chooses what it does: receive only, receive and measure the distance, or the same with another aircraft instead of a ground station.
controls.context: The T/R position gives distance and bearing. In the air-to-air modes the two aircraft must be on channels 63 apart. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: VOR/ILS PWR switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The receiver is off.

positions.name: PWR
positions.text: The receiver is on.

controls.text: This switch turns the VOR/ILS receiver on. With it on, the VOR or localizer and the marker beacon functions work.
controls.context: The manual says the switch positions are OFF and PWR. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: VOR/ILS frequency knobs (1 MHz and 50 kHz)
controls.text: These two knobs tune the VOR or ILS frequency. One sets the whole MHz (three digits), the other the steps of 50 kHz.
controls.context: A VOR is a ground radio beacon. The pilot reads the direction to it on the HSI. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: test button (first)
controls.text: The game names this button 'test'. The TACAN box and the VOR/ILS box each have a test button, and the game's label does not say which one this is. This is the first of the two (callout PNT_158 in the front cockpit).
controls.context: The manual says the TACAN test button runs a self-test of the TACAN set, and the VOR/ILS test button does the VOR and ILS self-test. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: test button (second)
controls.text: The game names this button 'test'. The TACAN box and the VOR/ILS box each have a test button, and the game's label does not say which one this is. This is the second of the two (callout PNT_166 in the front cockpit).
controls.context: The manual says the VOR/ILS test button does the VOR and ILS self-test, and the TACAN test button runs a self-test of the TACAN set. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: Cabin air, anti-ice and exterior-lights controls (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These controls on the right console look after the air in the cockpit, the heating of the pitot tubes and engine intakes, and the lights.
panels.context: The manual says the cabin pressure and temperature system works by itself, and the pilot only sets the wanted temperature. The anti-ice heaters are switched on in icing conditions. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: ANTI-ICE PITOT switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The pitot heater is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The pitot heater is off.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The heater is tested; ON shows on the indicator.

controls.text: This switch heats a pitot tube, a small tube on the nose that measures airspeed, so ice cannot block it. ON heats, OFF stops, TEST checks the heater.
controls.context: The manual says each cockpit has its own switch. The front switch also heats the angle-of-attack probe. The indicators show ON, OFF or stripes. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: Lights control panel (LIGHTS) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel switches the lights: the instrument and panel lights in the cockpit, and the lights on the outside of the plane.
panels.context: The manual says the cockpit lights are controlled on each right console and the outside lights from the front cockpit. The front panel is the main one. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: INST knob (instrument lights)
controls.text: Turning this knob turns on the lights inside the instruments and sets how bright they are.
controls.context: OFF switches the instrument lights off. The manual says the knob works together with the instrument panel lighting. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: CONSOLE knob (panel lights)
controls.text: Turning this knob turns on the lights of the control panels and sets their brightness.
controls.context: OFF switches the console lights off. The console lights are fed by the DC primary bus. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: FLOOD knob (cockpit flood lights)
controls.text: Turning this knob turns on the white flood lights that light up the cockpit and sets their brightness.
controls.context: The manual says the front cockpit has six flood lights and the rear cockpit has five, and they can be swivelled. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: WARN switch (BRT/DIM)

positions.name: BRT
positions.text: The warning lights are bright.

positions.name: DIM
positions.text: The warning lights are dimmed.

controls.text: This switch sets the brightness of the warning, caution and advisory lights, bright or dimmed.
controls.context: The pilot dims them for night flying. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: stick
areas.text: The rear control stick, with its trim switch.

panels.name: Control stick grip (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The control stick is the lever between the pilot's knees. Tilting it left and right rolls the plane, and moving it forward and back pitches the nose down and up. The buttons on the grip are used without taking a hand off it.
panels.context: Each cockpit has its own stick. The manual lists on the stick the trim switch, the rocket and bomb release button, the trigger, the gun camera and nose wheel steering button, and the radio transmit button. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Trim switch (4-way hat)
controls.text: This small four-way switch on top of the grip sets the trim. Trim is a steady push on the controls, so the pilot does not need to hold the stick. Forward and back move the elevator trim, left and right move the aileron trim.
controls.context: The manual says the trim switch moves the trim tabs of the ailerons and elevators and that the trim indicator shows the elevator trim. It springs back to the middle. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.
